theorem_title: Blindness is downward closed in the Boolean realization
natural_language_statement:
For arbitrary types $I,J$ and a Boolean family $F:J\times I\to\{0,1\}$, use the base-and-face observation system: the base has target 0 and all observations 0; face $j$ has target 1 and observation $1-F(j,i)$ at coordinate $i$. Let $S,T\subseteq I$ satisfy $S\subseteq T$. Then

$$
T\text{ is blind}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad S\text{ is blind}.
$$

Here blindness means that two states with different Boolean targets agree at every selected observation. The result expresses monotonicity under removal of observations.
